about.heading: About us
about.description: We are a Peruvian company innovating livestock farming with close, useful technology designed for the reality of the countryside.
about.description02: Since 2026 we have been developing ICHU: a platform that brings together each animal's information, herd signals and veterinary support to make timely decisions and better protect every production.
about.alternativeText: ICHU smart collar for livestock monitoring

problem.heading: The field has information.
problem.heading02: The challenge is turning it into decisions.
problem.introduction: Livestock work generates data every day. However, much of this knowledge is lost or stays fragmented.

issue01.title: Manual, scattered records
issue01.description: Field notebooks and loose notes that make it hard to rebuild each animal's complete, continuous history when it is urgently needed.

issue02.title: Late detection of changes
issue02.description: A drop in grazing, a thermal variation or isolation in the paddock is often noticed when the problem has already advanced, raising costs and risks.

issue03.title: Gap in veterinary visits
issue03.description: When the veterinarian reaches the pen, they often have to assess without the prior log of symptoms, applied doses or exact dates.

issue04.title: Pasture & water control
issue04.description: Supervising pasture rotation, water point availability and the location of animal groups across wide terrain requires constant time.

issue05.title: Cost & loss tracking
issue05.description: Keeping a clear count of extra forage, treatments and losses is complex when there is no organized structure for logging.

issue06.title: Team coordination
issue06.description: Difficulty aligning what field staff observe, what the manager logs and the guidelines given by the veterinary specialist.

productFlow.heading: A new way to understand livestock farming.
productFlow.introduction: ICHU is a platform designed to help farmers and veterinarians better organize and understand the information of each animal and the field.

step01.title: Animal
step01.description: Individually identified with its collar and traits.

step02.title: Data
step02.description: Temperature, movement, forage and event signals.

step03.title: Farmer
step03.description: Check the herd's overall status and receive early alerts.

step04.title: Veterinarian
step04.description: Access the full clinical history before and during the visit.

step05.title: Decision
step05.description: Preventive, timely actions that protect production.

productFlow.quotation: ICHU does not replace the veterinarian. It gives them more information to work with.
productFlow.context: Technology observes and collects patterns; professional judgment and livestock knowledge define the action.

animalLifecycle.heading: Every animal, one continuous story.
animalLifecycle.introduction: Livestock farming is not a static spreadsheet: it is a living biological cycle. ICHU organizes the key milestones of each animal's life to preserve its productive and health memory from its first days.

stage01.title: Identification
stage01.description: Collar assignment, genealogy, birth date and traits.

stage02.title: Activity
stage02.description: Observe grazing, movement and resting routines.

stage03.title: Feeding
stage03.description: Pasture rotation, mineral supplementation and water access.

stage04.title: Events
stage04.description: Log of heats, breedings, births, weanings or sudden changes.

stage05.title: Medical visit
stage05.description: On-site clinical review backed by data readings.

stage06.title: Treatment
stage06.description: Medication or vaccine application with dose logging.

technology.heading: Technology that observes.
technology.introduction: ICHU is being designed to progressively connect with telemetry and Internet of Things (IoT) devices built to withstand the climate and conditions of our geography.
technology.title: Body temperature
technology.description: Monitoring thermal oscillations to early identify feverish episodes, heat stress or metabolic alterations before visible symptoms.
technology.description02: Detection of physical activity levels, rumination, resting time or lethargy that may suggest discomfort, heat or onset of labor.
technology.description03: Location by sectors and paddocks to prevent losses from straying, optimize rotational grazing and safeguard livestock safety.

alerts.heading: Preventive alerts, not automatic diagnoses.
alerts.introduction: ICHU alerts work as a timely call to attention so the farmer or veterinarian can inspect the animal in time.

alert01.title: Activity change detected
alert01.description: Cow #089 logged 45% less movement during the last 6 hours of her usual grazing.

alert02.title: Temperature out of range
alert02.description: Bull #014 logged 39.4 °C sustained across two consecutive readings.

alert03.title: Animal outside its usual zone
alert03.description: Group of 3 heifers detected near the east perimeter fence.

alert04.title: Pending veterinary follow-up
alert04.description: Reminder of the second dose of treatment prescribed for Calf #201.

alerts.description: the alerts and metrics shown are conceptual orientation tools. They do not constitute an automated clinical diagnosis nor replace the professional judgment of the veterinarian.

propertyManagement.heading: It is also about understanding the countryside.
propertyManagement.introduction: The animal depends on its pastures, water and farm management. ICHU helps visualize the farm as an orderly operation.
propertyManagement.title: The whole farm in one view
propertyManagement.description: Manage forage rotation, plan water supplies and keep a live animal inventory without relying on loose sheets.
propertyManagement.alternativeText: Farm map with grazing paddocks, water points and pasture condition

regulatoryContext.heading: Technology designed for our livestock.
regulatoryContext.introduction: Livestock management involves health commitments and official regulations. ICHU seeks to facilitate the organization of useful information for productive and veterinary management, within the framework of the obligations applicable to each activity.
regulatoryContext.description: Ministry of Agrarian Development and Irrigation: livestock development policies, pastures and productive promotion.
regulatoryContext.description02: National Agricultural Health Service: official vaccination calendars, zoosanitary control and tagging.
regulatoryContext.description03: PPA (MIDAGRI): official registry for identification and access to State services.
